question: What if your agent could render the shot itself?

hook_visual.intent: the agent writing a scene, rendering it, then judging the image

points.claim: vork is a headless 3D and VFX engine built for agents: scenes are written as code and rendered on a GPU.
points.spoken: It's vork, a headless rendering engine built for agents: scenes are written as code and rendered on a GPU.
points.source_note: README: 'vork, the Voyager rendering kernel, is a headless 3D and VFX engine built for agents.' / 'These are scenes written as code and rendered on a GPU. No video model required.'

points.title: A renderer for agents

points.claim: There is no editor to drive: the agent writes a scene, renders a preview, looks at the image and revises the code.
points.spoken: There's no editor. The agent writes a scene, renders a preview, looks at the image and revises the camera and the light.
points.source_note: README: 'An agent writes a scene, renders it, looks at the result and revises the code. There is no editor to drive.'; 'Refine the camera and lighting before rendering at final quality.'

visual.intent: preview, inspect, revise camera and lighting

points.title: No editor to drive

youtube.title: Agent rendering: vork renders the shot without a video model
youtube.description: Agent 3D rendering without a video model: vork is a headless engine where a scene is a program, so the agent writes it, renders a preview on the GPU, looks at the image and revises camera and lighting. It exposes geometry, ray queries and GPU compute, which means a shader can be written in the middle of a shot, and the examples run to a million self-steering birds and VFX cut into real footage. Repo: https://github.com/voyager-so/vork #Shorts #3DRendering #VFX #AIAgents #Rust
